meta.purpose: open-text always-big-THINK baseline (latency+energy+accuracy) for the reframe; fills the missing 32B-think open-text cell

setup.accuracy_scorer: run_openvqa exact-match/contains modal_ok (same scorer as the open-text pipeline)
setup.accuracy_engine: vLLM tp=2, greedy (temp0, n_samples=1), max_tokens=512, n=200/dataset (first-200, paired by idx w/ existing no-think dumps in ckpts/openvqa/strong_lingshu)
setup.latency_engine: HF batch-1, single GPU, cap320 real vqa_rad images, per-visible-GPU NVML energy, n=15 after 3 warmup, max_new=1024 (SAME harness that produced the canonical no-think 665ms)

latency_energy_nothink_reference.source: logs/latency_opentext.jsonl via open_measure_latency_energy.py (GEN32), n=25; the deployed strong-leg number

verdict: open-text 32B THINK is ~16x slower and ~16x more energy than 32B no-think, and LOWER accuracy on all 3 perception datasets (pooled 0.387 think vs 0.537 no-think, delta -0.150). Reasoning overthinks open-text perception VQA -> always-big-THINK is a strictly worse strong leg than always-big-no-think on both cost and accuracy.
